newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks rally in morning, CITIC suspended.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks rally in morning, CITIC suspended.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks rallied in Tuesday morning trade, with talk that CITIC Pacific may buy a stake in Hong Kong utility China Light boosting sentiment.
The Hang Seng Index was up 115.17, or 0.87 percent, at 13,410.07, after rising to an early high of 13,450.56.
Turnover was HK$2.19 billion after the first hour of trade.
Trading in CITIC Pacific and China Light shares was suspended on Tuesday prompting rumours that CITIC may take a stake in China Light, brokers said.
"Everybody likes a takeover story in Hong Kong. It's something to take our mind off the (U.S.) bond market," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities.
Brokers said that as a mature power company with limited growth potential, China Light was an unusual target and not an obvious fit for CITIC.
Both companies declined to comment but promised announcements later. Shares in China Light rose HK$0.60 to HK$33.70 on Monday and CITIC Pacific added HK$1.10 to HK$39.50.
The suspensions prodded Hong Kong stocks into a buoyant mood, dispelling sour U.S. Treasuries which hampered the market at the opening.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell 21/32 on Monday to yield 6.94 percent ahead of Tuesday's release of the fourth-quarter U.S. employment cost index.
Bargain-hunting boosted shares of Hong Kong retailer Giordano after a slump of nearly 25 percent on Monday. The stock was up HK$0.35 at HK$4.15.
"I've got my eye on Giordano," said one trader. "I think the selling could be a little bit overdone."
Hongkong Electric was also favoured, rising HK$0.15 to HK$26.95.
Asia Securities International was the biggest gainer, rising HK$0.525, or 30 percent, to HK$2.275.
Among 983 issues traded, 393 advanced while 97 declined.
